brief: Democrats won the House and Senate, matching MS's 'cohesive' Democratic majority scenario. The reconciliation route is closed, removing the main upside risk to Treasury's borrowing needs; a possible SNAP/Medicaid delay adds only modest 2-7y issuance against a $2tn deficit, so front-end dynamics (the December 11 funding deadline, the 2027 debt limit, an x-date in late 3Q27) matter more. FX stays in MS's defense regime: long JPY/CHF/EUR, short AUD (AI sentiment exposure) and CAD (tariff risk), with NOK/SEK also pressured. MS keeps OW global equities vs UW core fixed income, arguing AI capex stays intact even as data-center-specific sentiment weakens. The clearest negative is data-center policy risk: Democrat Gina Hinojosa's Texas governorship win raises moratorium risk on new data-center approvals, and Amy Acton's Ohio win threatens a 10GW NVIDIA-linked project. MS revalues the exposed names: CIFR ($18/share existing assets, $51.50 target, $5 bear case), GLXY ($43 SOTP), NRG ($129 vs $96), CEG ($378 target), TLN ($430 vs $357), VST ($180 vs $140), with WMB a standing high-conviction buy on data-center power demand. Healthcare: a sweep favors Medicaid-focused CNC/MOH over diversified UNH/CVS, and pressures HUM.
